findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts:1023 — `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty Prisma `updateMany` payload; empty `data` has historically been rejected by Prisma ("Argument `data` must not empty") depending on version, and if the pinned version rejects it every Google Calendar availability lookup throws — pass `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly or drop the call

[Medium/performance] CalendarService.ts:1023 — the unconditional `UPDATE SelectedCalendar` (all rows for the credential) is added to the availability-lookup hot path (booking flow), adding write load and row-lock contention on shared credentials, and nothing in the PR reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` (the UI's "Last updated" comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so the write has no consumer

[Medium/bug] deleteCache.handler.ts:26 deletes via raw `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` instead of the existing `CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential()`, and connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly — both bypass the repository selection that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when calendar-cache is disabled (leaving the mock's `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` unreachable), and a non-Prisma backend (e.g., Redis-backed `ICalendarCacheRepository`) would have the wrong layer cleared/read and would fail to satisfy the extended interface

[Medium/bug] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:117 — the cache timestamp is rendered with a hardcoded `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the app locale available via `useLocale()` and the user's timezone preference, so all non-US users get US-formatted dates

[Medium/test_gap] No tests added for the new `deleteCache` mutation (notably the credential-ownership/authorization check), `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId`, or the new `CredentialActionsDropdown` component

[Low/bug] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:38 — `deleteCacheMutation` never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates in `onSettled`), so the "Last updated" value can remain stale after a delete whenever the optional `onSuccess` prop isn't wired to a refetch

[Low/api] deleteCache.handler.ts:23 — the not-found/no-access case throws a plain `Error`, which tRPC surfaces as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with a masked message; use `TRPCError` (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) so clients can distinguish authorization failures from server faults

[Low/data] migration 20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at backfills `updatedAt` to `NOW()` for all existing `CalendarCache` rows, so every pre-existing (potentially long-stale) cache entry displays "Last updated: <deploy time>" until rewritten — misleading status immediately after rollout

[Low/data] getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21 and repository/user.ts:899 — `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` are added to the selected-calendar types/selects but never consumed in this PR, and the internal `googleChannelId` (Google push-channel identifier) is serialized to the client unnecessarily if these objects flow into the `connectedCalendars` tRPC response

[Low/doc_defect] migration 20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:2 — the retained auto-generated warning ("Added the required column `updatedAt` … without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.") contradicts the hand-edited `DEFAULT NOW()` statement below it and misrepresents the migration as unsafe for populated tables
[Low/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:66 — `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; with GNU sed (Linux) the empty-string argument is consumed as the script and the substitution fails

[Low/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:8 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's CWD rather than the script's location, so running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root reads/creates a `.env` outside the repository

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] CalendarService.ts:1023 — the unconditional `UPDATE SelectedCalendar` (all rows for the credential) is added to the availability-lookup hot path (booking flow), adding write load and row-lock contention on shared credentials, and nothing in the PR reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` (the UI's "Last updated" comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so the write has no consumer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` in `CalendarService.ts` right after availability caching. This is a new write on a path that appears to run during availability lookups, and it updates *all* selected calendars for the credential, which can add write load/locking. Also, the new UI “Last updated” shown in `CredentialActionsDropdown` is sourced from `connectedCalendars.cacheUpdatedAt`, which is populated from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), not from `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so the added write isn’t clearly consumed by the new cache-status feature. However, the finding’s claim that nothing reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not strictly true within this diff because `UserRepository` now selects `updatedAt` on selected calendars.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both new code paths bypass the calendar-cache repository abstraction: `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` explicitly imports and instantiates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` (`new CalendarCacheRepository()`), and `deleteCache.handler.ts` directly calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany(...)` instead of going through an `ICalendarCacheRepository` method. The presence of `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` implementing `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` and logging “calendar-cache being disabled” suggests there is (or was intended to be) a swappable repository layer; these handlers won’t participate in that swapping. However, the PR diff does not show the actual repository-selection mechanism or a flag that swaps in the mock, so the claim that this is a runtime defect when cache is disabled or non-Prisma-backed cannot be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess?.()` (lines ~31-44) and does not invalidate/refetch `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, while `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates queries in `onSettled`. Since `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` now enriches results with `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache` and the UI displays “Last updated” from that field, deleting the cache via `deleteCache.handler.ts` (which `deleteMany`s rows) can leave the displayed cache status stale unless the caller wires `onSuccess` to trigger a refetch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] migration 20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at backfills `updatedAt` to `NOW()` for all existing `CalendarCache` rows, so every pre-existing (potentially long-stale) cache entry displays "Last updated: <deploy time>" until rewritten — misleading status immediately after rollout

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()` in the migration (`ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" ... DEFAULT NOW();`) and in Prisma (`@default(now()) @updatedAt`). The UI then displays cache freshness using the max `updatedAt` per credential (`CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groupBy `_max.updatedAt`, surfaced as `cacheUpdatedAt` and formatted in `CredentialActionsDropdown`). For pre-existing rows, `updatedAt` will be set to the migration execution time regardless of when the cache value was actually computed, so the displayed “Last updated” can be misleading right after rollout. This is a real, diff-grounded concern, but it’s more about data semantics/UX correctness than a runtime-breaking defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to selected-calendar typings (`packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts`) and to the Prisma select in `UserRepository` (`packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts`) without any corresponding usage shown elsewhere in this PR. That creates unnecessary DB selection/serialization risk. While the diff doesn’t conclusively prove these fields flow into the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` tRPC response, the concern about selecting an internal identifier (`googleChannelId`) without an evident need is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:8 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's CWD rather than the script's location, so running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root reads/creates a `.env` outside the repository

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is a relative path resolved against the caller’s current working directory. If the script is run from the repo root (e.g., `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), `../.env` points to a `.env` in the parent directory (outside the repo), and the script may create/modify that file (`touch`, `sed`, `echo >>`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavioral defect in the script.
